title: Repair Windows D3D12 capability and workload closure
requires: Physical Windows GTX 1080 with D3D12 and CUDA comparison access
scope: Repair the non-timing candidate-v10 Windows D3D12 exit blocker recorded by F8-27: the driver advertises only 46 of 49 required capabilities, omits the three separate-system liquid-liquid modes and rejects the six-family mixed workload. Preserve shared Slang physics, the sole fixed-tick schedule, API 0.3, driver ABI 2 and CUDA behavior. This is repair work for a replacement candidate; it does not mutate or relabel candidate-v10 evidence.
acceptance: Reproduce the exact F8-27 capability reduction and workload rejection before changing source, retaining installed driver, SDK, device and manifest identities.

Expose contact, pressure and viscosity for separate liquid systems through ordinary D3D12 public execution without platform-specific physics equations, CPU fallback, capability spoofing or a private qualification path.

Pass all 49 capability obligations, 30 public cases, 12 physical scenarios, lifecycle/recovery assertions, independent work budgets and five negative controls in plain and validation modes on the physical D3D12 target.

Preserve one 1/60 advance, one shared spatial publication, bounded solver work and the existing dispatch, submission, readback and synchronization ceilings. No hidden substep, retry or alternate schedule is permitted.
Run the affected Windows CUDA, portable shader, SDK relocation and installed Gallery regressions. Publish exact-source artifacts and classify timing and scene-quality results separately.
